source.title: Do tabular foundation models repair themselves?

page_placements.theme: Redundant parallel pathways rather than active compensation: removing one component, edge or layer changes little, removing several together changes much

record.file_problem: The full post text is present. Some equations and table headings appear to have lost symbols in the web text, but the reported results are legible.
record.tranche_reason: It applies the total-effect/direct-effect causal framework used for the Hydra effect to new models and a new setting, tabular foundation models, and reports outcomes of layer ablations.
record.gate_note: The study directly measures layer-ablation total and direct effects and reports repaired-region proportions and per-model fits. It does not measure later layers' activation changes directly; compensation is assessed through the total/direct-effect comparison. Results quoted from McGrath et al. and Balef et al. are prior-work results and are not extracted as rows. Figure 5 has no separately reported numerical point values, so only the study's textual description and the accompanying table are used.
record.test_reason: It applies McGrath et al.'s total/direct-effect test for layer-level compensation to a new kind of transformer: four tabular foundation models (TFMs) under resample ablation. It reports how often layers are repaired and per-layer CE-vs-DE fits. The method matches the original, but the system type (tabular models, not language models) and the output (correct-label logit margin) are new, so T3 fits better than T1.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find weak or no evidence of layer-wise self-repair in the four TFMs, with redundancy more prevalent. They caution that the study covers few models and datasets and only binary classification, and that why TE≈0 remains unclear.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the total/direct-effect causal framework, but tests tabular foundation models with resample ablation and correct-versus-wrong-label logit margin rather than the language-model setting described for Hydra.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by model: repaired-region shares range from 0% to 11%, and the reported CE-versus-DE fit values and slopes differ across models. The study also notes its conclusions are limited to the selected models, datasets, and binary classification setting.

fits_no_version.finding: In TFMs, layer ablations mostly look redundant (TE≈0 and DE≈0) rather than repaired. The redundancy share reaches 78% in TabFM.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness to layer ablation in some transformers reflects redundancy rather than active downstream compensation.

record.problems: The study uses only 4 models, 15 binary classification datasets, and capped context/test samples; the authors call for more models, tasks, and datasets. No uncertainty estimates are reported. Some equation and table-heading symbols are missing in the web text.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric Figure 5 point values are reported in the text, so no figure-only point rows were extracted. Prior-study results and the cited Balef et al. results were excluded.

untested.parts: Language models; ablation of attention layers specifically (the study ablates whole transformer layers); direct measurement of later layers' activation changes.
Not tested: no late-MLP or maximum-likelihood-token erasure analysis.
Not tested: no per-input variance or overcorrection analysis.
Uses only resample ablation and does not compare it with zero ablation in the same setup. It shows no self-repair to compare, so V6 is not tested.
Discussed as motivation only; attribution error is not measured.

missing.what: Qualitative Figure 5 result: no point mass lies below the TE-vs-DE diagonal in any of the four TFMs. This contrasts with the original's below-diagonal pattern.
missing.locator: Our findings, Figure 5 and text 'very few points below the TE-vs-DE diagonal'

record.verdict_notes: This is a non-peer-reviewed LessWrong post with no uncertainty estimates. The Chinchilla 7B row in the fit table is a cited result and is correctly excluded. The sign convention for the CE-vs-DE slope is internally inconsistent: CE = TE − DE implies a negative slope under repair, yet the authors expect a positive one. This weakens how the fit rows (r5–r8) can be read; the region proportions are the more reliable evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Tests layer-wise compensation in tabular foundation models, not attention-layer-only ablations in language models; does not directly report later attention-layer outputs.
No late-MLP maximum-likelihood-token erasure or earlier-component ablation comparison.
No single-head ablations, full-distribution language-model measures, or language-model family/size comparison.
Does not test prompt-level variation or overcorrection in language models.
Does not identify or test backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons.
Uses resample ablation in tabular models, but does not test language-model self-repair under mean/resample ablations or compare against zero ablation in the same experiment.
Does not measure ablation-based importance scores or their attribution error.

rows.check: With CE = TE − DE, full repair (TE≈0) gives CE ≈ −DE, a slope near −1. So TabICL's slope of −0.41 with fit 0.58 could reflect partial compensation under that convention. relationships.condition: Tabular foundation models (LimiX-2M, Mitra, TabICL-v2, TabFM), whole-layer resample ablation, 15 binary classification datasets
relationships.reason: Repaired shares are 0–11% while redundancy dominates (16–78%) (r1–r4). Per-layer CE-vs-DE fits are near zero for three models (r5, r6, r8). Layer-level compensation does not carry over to this non-language transformer setting.
relationships.display_finding: Repair accounted for 0–11% versus 16–78% redundancy, with little layerwise compensation in these tabular foundation models.

statements.correction: Mitra: 2% repaired, state partial. TabFM: 2% repaired, state partial. TabICL-v2: 0% repaired, state absent. Overall evidence described as weak.
statements.problem: The numbers match, but calling Mitra and TabFM absent overstates their nonzero repaired shares.
Redundancy exceeds repair in every model, but it is a majority only in TabFM; most points are classified as others in the other three models.
